sections.h2: How do I sell my house fast in Houston?
sections.html:
Houston sellers can list with an agent, sell privately, or take a cash offer, and the right choice depends on how much time and repair money you have. With a population the Texas State Historical Association says passed every other Texas city by 1930, Houston is a market of its own: the Census Bureau estimates 2,397,315 residents as of July 1, 2025, so no two neighborhoods price alike.

Because the city is so large and has so many renters, a seller should know who is likely to buy. QuickFacts shows only 42.1% of Houston homes are owner-occupied, which means investors, landlords and first-time buyers all compete for houses. A cash offer works well for a house with deferred maintenance, flood damage, a tenant or a title issue.

  • Pull your deed and any survey, and find out whether your street has deed restrictions.
  • Check which appraisal district and taxing units apply to your address.
  • Get at least two written offers, each with a closing date.

sections.h2: What should a Houston seller know about the city's history and land rules?
sections.html:
Houston began on August 30, 1836, when two brothers advertised the Town of Houston, and the Texas State Historical Association says it became the state's largest city by 1930. The Houston Ship Channel opened in 1914, oil refineries followed, and the city annexed older suburbs in the late 1940s and again in later decades. By 2015 the city covered 627 square miles, per the Association, and the Census Bureau lists 640.44 square miles of land for 2020.

The most useful fact for a seller is that Houston has no zoning. The Association says voters rejected it, and that deed restrictions on subdivisions control most construction. A deed restriction can limit what you build and how a lot is used, so read yours before you sell, and tell the buyer about them.

The city's planning department adds that a plat, which is a surveyed map of the lot, is required before building permits, and that single-family designation can allow a duplex or a garage apartment under 900 square feet unless deed restrictions say otherwise. The city also reviews plats in an extraterritorial area about five miles beyond its limits, where its permit and inspection rules do not apply.

sections.h2: What does Census data say about Houston housing?
sections.html:
QuickFacts gives a median value of $277,800 for owner-occupied homes in Houston in 2020 to 2024, with median monthly owner costs of $2,240 for those with a mortgage. The city has 930,404 households.

The median rent of $1,361 and the 42.1% ownership rate show a deep rental market, which is useful if you are selling an investment house. A seller with a tenant should know the lease terms and notice rules before accepting any offer.

sections.h2: How do Harris Central Appraisal District values affect my sale?
sections.html:
The Harris Central Appraisal District values most Houston property for tax purposes, and its site lets owners file protests, renditions and homestead exemptions online. It also offers an Exemption Wizard to show which exemptions may apply, and a deed protection feature that lets you register your home with the Harris County Clerk to help guard against deed fraud.

A few state rules shape the yearly cycle. Values are set as of January 1, notices for homesteads go out around April 1, and a protest is due by May 15 or 30 days after the notice arrives, whichever is later. After the review board rules, an owner can go to district court, binding arbitration, or the State Office of Administrative Hearings when the board value is over $1,000,000. An owner who appeals generally has to pay the undisputed tax before the delinquency date.

  • Homestead appraisal growth is capped at 10% a year once the exemption has been in place.
  • Heirs who are not on a recorded deed must file an affidavit of ownership, a death certificate and a recent utility bill to get the exemption.
  • A buyer who takes title after January 1 may claim the exemption for the rest of the year if the seller did not.

Check your tax bill to confirm which appraisal district and taxing units cover your parcel.

sections.h2: What about flooding and drainage when I sell a Houston house?
sections.html:
Flood history is a fact buyers and lenders ask about in Houston. The Texas State Historical Association describes the city as a place where paving and fast runoff have caused flooding, with severe floods in 1929 and 1935 leading to the Harris County Flood Control District and later to the Addicks and Barker reservoirs.

The city's planning department says flood mitigation, drainage, water and sewer are not part of the Planning Commission's plat review, so a house's flood risk is not settled by a plat. Ask the city and county for flood records on your address, gather any repair records and insurance claims, and share them with buyers. The same source cites about 48 inches of yearly rainfall, high humidity and summer averages near 94 degrees, conditions that wear on roofs, siding and air conditioning. A cash buyer will take a house with damage as is, but a clear record helps both sides agree on a price.

sections.h2: How do eviction, probate and tax sale rules affect a Houston sale?
sections.html:
If a tenant occupies the house, Texas requires at least three days' written notice to vacate unless the lease says otherwise, and an eviction suit is filed in justice court. The State Law Library says the hearing is set between 10 and 21 days after filing, and a tenant may appeal to county court within five days of judgment. A writ of possession cannot issue until six days after the final judgment.

For an inherited house, note that Texas repealed its inheritance tax effective September 1, 2015, per a Comptroller notice. Probate must generally be started within four years of death. A small estate affidavit is limited to estates of $75,000 or less outside the homestead.

If taxes are behind, the lien that attached on January 1 stays on the house. Penalty and interest begin February 1, and a taxing unit may sue and sell the property at auction. The County Clerk records deeds, and the Harris County Clerk's records office holds recorded plats, which you can request by email or phone through the city's plat page.

faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists 640.44 square miles of land in 2020 and 2,397,315 residents in 2025. Confirm the county and appraisal district for your own address before you rely on a tax figure.

faqs.q: Does Houston have zoning that limits what I can do with my house?
faqs.a: No citywide zoning. The Texas State Historical Association says voters rejected it. Private deed restrictions and city plat and permit rules still apply, so read your restrictions.

faqs.q: Can I protest my Houston property value?
faqs.a: Yes. File with the appraisal review board by May 15, or within 30 days after your notice is delivered if that is later. The Harris Central Appraisal District site offers online filing.

faqs.q: Where do I get a plat of my lot?
faqs.a: Plats are filed with the Harris County Clerk's records office after approval. The City of Houston planning site also has a map viewer and Plat Tracker for looking up applications by address.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Houston?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports $277,800 for owner-occupied homes for 2020 to 2024. That covers the whole city, so use a written offer or appraisal for your own house.
